{{Short description|Type of positive integer pairs}}
{{No footnotes|date=September 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[number theory]], '''betrothed numbers''' or '''quasi-amicable numbers''' are two positive [[integer]]s such that the [[addition|sum]] of the [[proper divisor]]s of either number is one more than the value of the other number. In other words, (''m'',&nbsp;''n'') are a pair of betrothed numbers if ''s''(''m'') =&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1  and s(''n'') =&nbsp;''m''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1, where s(''n'') is the [[aliquot sum]] of&nbsp;''n'': an equivalent condition is that σ(''m'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;σ(''n'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''m''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1, where σ denotes the [[sum-of-divisors function]].

The first few pairs of betrothed numbers are: (48,&nbsp;75), (140,&nbsp;195), (1050,&nbsp;1925), (1575,&nbsp;1648), (2024,&nbsp;2295), (5775,&nbsp;6128), which (removing brackets) may be sorted by magnitude {{OEIS|id=A005276}}.

All known pairs of betrothed numbers have opposite [[Parity (mathematics)|parity]].  Any pair of the same parity must exceed 10<sup>13</sup>.

== Quasi-sociable numbers ==
Quasi-sociable numbers or reduced sociable numbers are numbers whose [[aliquot sum]]s minus one form a cyclic sequence that begins and ends with the same number. They are generalizations of the concepts of betrothed numbers and [[quasiperfect number]]s. The first quasi-sociable sequences, or quasi-sociable chains, were discovered by Mitchell Dickerman in 1997:
 
* <math>1215571544 = 2^3\cdot 11\cdot 13813313</math>
* <math>1270824975 = 3^2\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 19\cdot 42467</math>
* <math>1467511664 = 2^4\cdot 19\cdot 599\cdot 8059</math>
* <math>1530808335 = 3^3\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 1619903</math>
* <math>1579407344 = 2^4\cdot 31^2\cdot 59\cdot 1741</math>
* <math>1638031815 = 3^4\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 521\cdot 1109</math>
* <math>1727239544 = 2^3\cdot 2671\cdot 80833</math>
* <math>1512587175 = 3\cdot 5^2\cdot 11\cdot 1833439</math>
